deep.reconstruction:
WHAT THE PAGE IS. This is one sheet of Gauss's working tables of classes of positive binary quadratic forms ax^2+2bxy+cy^2 of negative determinant b^2-ac = -p. Each column heading 'p . h' gives a prime p and the class number h of properly primitive forms of determinant -p, i.e. h(-4p) in modern terms.

Every prime on the page is ≡ 5 (mod 8): 2437, 2389, 2381, 2357, 2341, 2333, 2309, 2293, 2269, 2237, 2221. The primes ≡ 1 (mod 8) in the same range (2273, 2281, 2297, 2377, 2393, 2417) are absent. The neighbouring pages continue the same sequence downward (2749 ... 2477 before; 2213 ... 1949 after).

HOW A COLUMN IS BUILT. For each p Gauss picks a small form F = (a1, b1) with b1^2 ≡ -p (mod a1). For p = 2381, 2357, 2333 and 2309 this is (3, 1).
- Row k records the first coefficient a, often with a middle coefficient b, of a reduced representative of F^k.
- b is given only modulo a, not necessarily as the reduced value. Example for 2381, row 9: (50, 37) ~ (50, -13, 51).
- The column stops at k = h/2. There the ambiguous class (2, 1, (p+1)/2) appears, since 1 + p = 2c. So F has order h, and Cl(-4p) is cyclic.
- The rows past h/2 are not needed: F^(h-k) is the inverse of F^k (same a, b -> -b).
- So the number of rows (h/2 + 1) is the evidence for the class number written in the heading.

Sample checks (b^2 + p = a*c in every case; all verified):
- 2381: (3,1), (9,7), (27,7), (30,23), (10,3), (30,13), (47,4), (17,13), (50,37), (25,13), (34,21); then 45, 15, 5, 15, 45, 18, 6, 2. So h = 38.
- 2357: (3,1), (9,1), (27,10), (46,9), (39,23), (13,10), (39,10), (21,11), (7,4), (21,4), (42,17), (14,3), (42,31); ... 26, 23, 18, 6, 2. So h = 42.
- 2341: generator (7,2): (49,16), (10,3), (41,18), (43,29), (25,3), (26,21), (13,5), (47,3), (37,29), 35, (5,2), 35, (14,5), 2. So h = 30.
- 2333: (3,1), (9,4), (27,4), (29,25), (34,9), (41,39), (19,2), (46,17), 23, ...; rows 13-17 are continued at the top of the next column. So h = 34.
- 2309: (3,1), (9,7), (27,16), (30,11), (10,1), (30,1), (35,29), (38,3), (31,4), (25,21), (42,29), (14,1), (42,1), (33,23), (11,1), (33,1), (35,1), 22, ..., (15,14), (5,4), (15,4), 18, 6, 2. So h = 66. Note that 2310 = 2·3·5·7·11, so every small prime splits, which explains the large h.
- 2293: generator (19,5): (17,6), 31, (37,1), (34,11), (38,33), (2,1). So h = 14.
- 2221: generator (10,3): (25,23), 11, 43, 37, 22, 50, (5,2), (2,1). So h = 18.
- 2389: generator (10,1): (25,6), (11,3), 37, (26,9), ... 50, 5, 2. So h = 34. Rows 6, 8, 9 show corrected first coefficients.
- 2269 (h = 30) and 2237 (h = 30) are given mostly by first coefficients only. Part of 2269 is covered by ink blots.

THE NON-CYCLIC CASE p = 2437 (marked *). Here the rows are indexed i.j:
- 0.0 = 1; 0.1 = (11,4); 0.2 = (22,7); 0.3 = (2,1). So A = (11,4) has order 6.
- 1.0 = (29,12), 1.1 = (23,22), 1.2 = (41,33), then 46, 47, ... These are B·A^j with B = (29,12) of order 3, outside <A>.
- So Cl ≅ Z/6 × Z/3, h = 18. Listing classes up to inversion needs 4 + 6 = 10 entries = (18 + 2)/2, which matches.
- The principal genus has type 3×3, so this is an 'irregular determinant' in the sense of Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (DA) art. 306.
- The footnote '1* 3.6.18' summarises this: one irregular determinant in the batch, of type 3·6, h = 18.

SIDE COMPUTATION 1: SUMS OF THREE SQUARES (column 2341). The triples written beside the even rows are representations of 2341 as x^2+y^2+z^2:
- 46,15,0; 33,26,24; 42,24,1; 46,12,9; 39,26,12; 48,6,1; 44,18,9; 39,28,6.
- These are 8 essentially distinct representations. With signs and orders they give 1·24 + 7·48 = 360 = 12·h(-4·2341) = 12·30.
- They are attached one-to-one to the 8 classes (up to inversion) of the principal genus, the even powers F^0, F^2, ..., F^14. Indeed (7/2341) = -1, so F lies in the non-principal genus and its even powers form the principal genus.
- This is the DA art. 291-292 correspondence between three-square representations and binary classes, checked numerically.

SIDE COMPUTATION 2: DETERMINANT -2527 (column 2237). The triples on the right are forms (a, b, c) with a*c - b^2 = 2527:
- (1,0,2527), (8,5,319), (16,9,163), (32,1,79), (43,15,64), (37,10,71), (11,5,232), (29,24,107), (23,16,121).
- This is preparatory work for D = 2527 = 7·19^2. That determinant is listed in the 2357 column with '2.10', i.e. 2 genera of 10 classes.

SIDE COMPUTATION 3: A TABLE FOR 2500-2600 (columns 2381 and 2357). These columns also list determinants D between 2500 and 2600, stepping alternately by 6 and 9.
- Both lists consist of D not divisible by 3 or 5 with D ≡ ±2 (mod 5).
- The 2381 list has D ≡ 2 (mod 3): 2507, 2513, 2522, ..., 2597. It carries no data yet.
- The 2357 list has D ≡ 1 (mod 3): 2503, 2512, ..., 2593. It carries entries 'g.k', read as number of genera . classes per genus. Examples: 2503 -> 1.21; 2512 = 16·157 -> 4.6; 2527 -> 2.10.
- Asterisks at 2542 and 2563 are probably irregularity flags (my interpretation, unverified).

BOTTOM-RIGHT TALLY. '10. 66.42.38.34.34.30.30.30.18.14 / 336.' This is the count (10) and the sum (336) of the class numbers h of the ten regular primes on this page; 2437 is excluded and handled separately.
- The mean is 33.6. The sum 336 requires 34 to be counted twice (2389 and 2333).
- All these h are ≡ 2 (mod 4), as they must be for p ≡ 5 (mod 8).
- The previous page's tally works the same way: 14 values, sum 656, mean 46 6/7.
- '(24.992)' is an unexplained comparison figure. Perhaps it is an expected average, but this is unclear.

PEN TRIALS. 'Problema / Theorema / Lemma / Theor.', 'Pars I', 'Rosma', 'x y', 'Yy', 'Ryz' have no mathematical content.
errors: 2389 column: rows 6, 8, 9 carry struck-out first coefficients (13 -> 38, 23 -> 46, 41 -> 23). These are corrected slips in the power sequence. 13 is a legitimate divisor (-2389 is a QR mod 13) but was misplaced.
The tally line shows one of the two 34's apparently struck out, yet the total 336 is correct only if both are counted. The deletion mark is either a slip or a smudge.
Entries such as (50,37), (29,24,107) and (23,16,121) are not in reduced form; the middle coefficient is only given mod a. This is a notation convention, not an error.
No arithmetic errors were found in the entries I checked. All checked (a, b) satisfy b^2 + p ≡ 0 (mod a); all eight three-square sums equal 2341; all nine -2527 forms satisfy ac - b^2 = 2527.

results.what: Tables of reduced representatives of successive powers of a generating class, for determinant -p with p ≡ 5 (mod 8), terminating at the ambiguous class (2,1,(p+1)/2). This gives h(-4p) and shows Cl is cyclic.
results.modern_name: Class number / class group computation for imaginary quadratic orders of discriminant -4p (cyclic structure via a generator)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae 1801; Nachlass class-number tables, Werke II)

results.what: Determinant -2437: class group Z/6 × Z/3 (h = 18) with non-cyclic principal genus, flagged as the one irregular determinant of the batch.
results.modern_name: Non-cyclic class group / 3-rank 2 of Q(sqrt(-2437)); Gauss's 'irregular determinant'

results.what: The eight essentially distinct representations of 2341 as a sum of three squares, matched with the 8 principal-genus classes up to inversion. Total count 360 = 12·h(-4·2341).
results.modern_name: Gauss's three-squares theorem r3(n) = 12 h(-4n) for squarefree n ≡ 1, 2 mod 4 (here n ≡ 5 mod 8)

results.what: Forms of determinant -2527 = -7·19^2, and a table of genera × classes-per-genus for determinants 2503-2593.
results.modern_name: Class number tables for negative discriminants (non-fundamental included)

results.what: Sum and mean of class numbers over a batch of primes ≡ 5 (mod 8): 10 values, sum 336, mean 33.6.
results.modern_name: Empirical average order of class numbers
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (DA art. 302 asymptotic; later Lipschitz, Mertens)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of Gauss's well-known class-number tables (published in part in Werke II from the Nachlass). Generator-power tables, the irregular determinant 2437 and the three-squares check all instantiate results in the Disquisitiones. It is a valuable record of method, but nothing new is attributed.
